memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "In the first row there shall be a ruby, a topaz and a beryl; in the second row a turquoise, a lapis lazuli and an emerald; in the third row a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst; in the fourth row a topaz, an onyx and a jasper. Mount them in gold filigree settings. There are to be twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." - Exodus 28:17b-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Twelve different stones, each one distinct — ruby, topaz, emerald, amethyst, jasper. No two alike. And each bore the name of a different tribe, engraved like a seal. God did not choose twelve identical stones. He chose twelve different ones, and every tribe got its own.

That variety is deliberate and beautiful. Judah was not turquoise; Judah was Judah, with its own stone, its own name, its own place on the breastpiece. Each tribe was known individually, not lumped into an anonymous mass. God does not deal with His people as a category. He knows names.

Jesus said that the good shepherd calls his own sheep by name and leads them out (John 10:3). You are not a face in the crowd to God. Your particular temperament, history, gifts, and struggles are known to Him. Nor should we flatten one another into sameness — God evidently likes variety among His people. Take comfort today: the God of the universe knows your name, and He has a place for you that no one else fills.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I believe God knows me personally and by name?
Am I valuing the difference in other believers, or expecting everyone to be like me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know me by name and gave me my own place among Your people. Thank You for knowing me personally. Help me value the differences You have placed in others. Amen.
